steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square vehicle portrait for a grounded American post-apocalyptic tabletop RPG.
Reference image: painting style, realistic weathering and neutral daylight ONLY; create a completely different vehicle.
Subject: an unoccupied broad, squat military four-by-four utility truck, a generic 1980s-style American military vehicle with a flat wide hood, low square four-door hard-top cabin, rear enclosed utility compartment, and a circular open roof hatch ring WITHOUT any gun or mount arm. Sand-beige paint worn to grey-green primer, restrained rust on seams, dusty glass, black chunky off-road tyres, utilitarian steel bumpers. Exactly four road wheels on two axles; physically correct proportions. No roof cargo, no spare tyre on the body, no mounted weapon. Hood and all four doors intact; no improvised armour, spikes or fantasy modifications. Left-hand drive.
Composition: full vehicle in a front three-quarter view, front facing lower-left, parked on a broken highway shoulder beside a weathered guardrail, dry weeds, scattered stones and cracked asphalt. Entire silhouette and wheels inside frame, vehicle occupies about 80 percent of image. No people, animals, markings, numbers, flags, insignia, letters, logos or plate characters. The roof hatch is a modest circular ring near the middle of the cabin, visibly open and empty. Avoid a tall turret. Natural neutral daylight, subdued earth palette, realistic materials and painterly detail matching the supplied sedan portrait. A practical surviving military utility truck, solid and used, not a burned wreck. Square 1024x1024 composition, opaque background.

Use case: sketch-to-render
Asset type: ROOF_OFF overhead vehicle token, isolated with genuine transparent alpha.
Image 1: AUTHORITATIVE layout and proportions guide, a simple SVG raster. Image 2: the vehicle's established portrait, identity/material reference ONLY.
Turn image 1 into the beautifully detailed painterly overhead version of the sand-beige military utility truck in image 2. Preserve image 1's component centres, spacing, wheel positions, broad rectangular shape, front-down orientation and straight orthographic camera. Remove the grey background to actual transparency.
GEOMETRY, non-negotiable: one single vehicle, long axis vertical, FRONT at BOTTOM. Exactly FOUR chunky black tyres, on TWO axles. Rear pair centred at y22.4%; front pair at y81.1%. Each pair projects clearly beyond the fenders, roughly y16%-29% and y75%-88%. NO wheels at the mirrors, no middle tyres, no tandem axle, no spare wheels. Four empty individual olive fabric bucket seats, two front and two rear, all facing down. Image-right seats and image-left seats have centres x71.1% and x28.9%; rear cushions around y39%; front cushions y57%. Keep the compact physically plausible legroom and seat proportions in the guide. Wide raised centre tunnel between both seat columns, gear controls toward the front. A square nonslip standing platform at x50%, y46.7% is the fifth crew position under a removable roof hatch: it is NOT a fifth seat, do not add a chair. Steering wheel at x71%, y64%, image-right, ahead of driver's chair; low broad dashboard around y67%. Empty ribbed rear cargo floor at y8%-28%, behind the four seats, with a low transverse partition. Hood at y70%-94%, front bumper/headlights at bottom. A tiny rear exhaust outlet near x25%,y3%.
CUTAWAY: completely remove ALL roof panels, including cargo-compartment roof, ALL glazing including front/rear/side windows, ALL upper pillars, upper door frames and hatch ring. Show lower doors, sill metal, wheel arches, open cargo floor, seats, tunnel, footwells and dashboard. The cabin and rear cargo are one large visible cutaway, only low partitions. No narrow leftover metal strips across the cabin. All glass and upper walls are absent, not transparent overlays.
Materials: dusty sand-beige body, grey-green primer showing through chipped edges, restrained rust, four clearly readable oversized off-road tyres with rugged tread, olive canvas cushions, dark worn floor, textured military controls. Same utilitarian identity and grounded painterly realism as portrait. Add detail to the simple guide without inventing mechanical assemblies or moving furniture. Four normal seats with plausible human proportions, readable as tabletop art.
Frame: keep image 1's 1:2 canvas (450x900 proportions), entire vehicle and mirrors inside, 3% clear margin at top/bottom, no ground or external cast shadow. True transparent background, no checkerboard painted in. No people, occupants, weapons, roof, hatch ring, cargo props, lettering, logos, emblems, numbers, plate characters, ring, base or watermark. This is the approved-geometry base that a matching roof will later cover.

steps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: matching ROOF_ON state for a tabletop overhead vehicle token.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the established roof-off vehicle. Image 2 is a REFERENCE ONLY for the appearance of its four-door hard-top roof and hatch. Keep image 1's exact scale, frame, orthographic camera and ALL existing exterior geometry and furniture positions.
Add ONLY the removable upper body assembly above the open cargo/cabin: a sand-beige hard roof over the rear cargo floor and four seats, side glazing with modest thin window frames and upper pillars, a rear window at the top/rear, and the wide dark front windshield immediately above the existing dashboard/steering wheel. Entire utility compartment is enclosed as in the portrait: no open pickup bed remains. Keep a broad continuous low roof, not a raised turret.
A circular OPEN EMPTY roof hatch ring sits precisely above image 1's square central standing pad between the seat rows, centre x50%, y43% of the whole image. Outer diameter about 26% of image WIDTH; opening about 20%. Through this one hole see the existing centre pad/tunnel in the SAME position, with a dark rim/interior. No fifth chair, weapon, ammunition, periscope or extra turret. The hatch ring is a modest metal lip, not tall armoured walls.
Furniture registration is critical: four seats stay exactly where they are in image 1, hidden behind the opaque roof wherever covered. Through glass, show only the parts that the true overhead projection permits. Do not move seats forward to put headrests into the front windshield. The windshield shows the established steering wheel, dashboard and front footwell areas at their original positions. Do not invent extra seats, different row spacing or a different console.
LOCKED REGIONS: keep image 1's hood, grille, headlights, bumpers, tiny rear exhaust, mirrors, lower doors, paint details outside the cabin, and tyre geometry unchanged. It has exactly FOUR large black tyres on TWO axles, rear pair near y23%, front pair near y78%. Keep these exact four tyres at their current positions, conspicuously visible beyond the body, no wheels below the mirrors and no extra middle pair. No spare tyres.
Orientation FRONT DOWN; entire vehicle centered in exactly the same 1:2 canvas and scale as image 1, with identical transparent margins. Genuine transparent alpha outside the truck. Preserve the painterly surface treatment and chipped sand paint, grey-green primer and olive interior. No occupants, ground, ground shadow, text, letters, numbers, flags, insignia, logos, plates with characters, framing, watermark or detached parts. The image must align with image 1 when toggled: change only the roof, windows and upper pillars.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Image 1: EDIT TARGET, the established roof-on military utility truck. Image 2: roof-off reference for the position of its square central standing pad. This is one SMALL LOCAL geometry correction, not a redesign.
Move ONLY the circular hatch opening and its metal ring DOWNWARD toward the front by about 4.5 percent of the full image HEIGHT (roughly 80 pixels in this source). Its current centre is near x50%, y38.5%; the required centre is x50%, y43%. The centre of the circular hole must sit directly above the centre of image 2's square checkerplate standing pad. The entire square pad should appear centered inside the hole, not cut off along the lower/front edge as it currently is. Preserve the ring's diameter and materials. Fill the ring's old upper location with the same continuous sand-beige roof surface and aligned roof ribs; remove the old opening completely so exactly one hatch remains. The roof and ring are viewed straight from above.
The space seen through the moved opening must be the ORIGINAL tunnel and square pad of image 2 in their unchanged positions. Do not move the square pad, console, floor or any furniture to meet the old hole. Move the ring instead.
Keep all other regions unchanged: the four tyres and two axles, exterior silhouette, hood, grille, bumpers, roof perimeter, side glazing, front windshield and ALL existing partial seat/steering-wheel/gear-lever glimpses through it. Do not repaint or enlarge windshield furniture. No extra tyre, chair, window, gun, weapon, person, object, label, text or emblem. FRONT remains DOWN, same exact canvas and scale, preserve actual transparent alpha. Change only the small old/new hatch roof region.
